technical_summary: SMB ecommerce company using chat-based product finder + embeddings for search. Mostly public-cloud hosted_api usage. Primary need: reduce perceived chat latency for EU customers. They send multi-turn contexts (~800-1,200 tokens typical), average generation ~80-250 tokens. Cost sensitive — prefer tips that don't require Dedicated capacity.
performance_findings: Observations from logs: elevated tail latency correlated with longer context lengths and simultaneous bursts during midday EU traffic. No KV-cache configured on their client; all requests go cold. Client-side timeout defaults 10s, but UI retries at 15s which sometimes causes duplicate traffic and queueing. They use model variant 'redwood-small-v1' (hosted) with default routing to nearest region but DNS caching pointed to eu-central for some users.
recommended_actions_shared_with_customer: 1) Region: recommend forcing eu-west endpoint for EU users or implement geo-aware routing in CDN; 2) Timeouts: set client read timeout to 8s, use streaming + early partial renders for UX; 3) Prompt length: truncate nonessential history beyond last 6 messages and use summary tokens for long threads; 4) Batching: enable small request-level batching for reranks/embeddings where possible; 5) Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated queries (products, FAQs); 6) Retries: exponential backoff with jitter, max retries 2, avoid synchronous retries that block UI; 7) Instrumentation: add request_id header and send samples to RW-4521 for deeper trace correlation.
